If I want to draw/write/read, I'd have a place to sit. As much as I love nature, I don't want to sit on the ground with the little creatures that will bite me. We have some smaller stools that my children use for marshmallow roasting, but they're too small for me. Since this one is considered XL, I thought it might be a better fit for me. It's not. It's still small. While it's slightly bigger than my children's other ones, it's not by much. My children have even complained about how uncomfortable this one is. I had decided to have it around for a reading chair(so my children could bring it wherever I'm doing chores or sitting and read to me), but two of them have already fallen out of it(it slipped beneath them). The first time was when one of my children was laughing at a book and I joked with him that he was laughing so hard, he fell out of his chair. One of my other children fell, too, though, after that. I think it won't be a big deal if it's on the ground or carpet, but on a flatter surface, like hardwood floor, it slips out from under a smaller person(at least), easily. Overall, with this one being considered an XL stool, we've been disappointed with it, but it does still provide a lightweight sitting option for when needed.

text_fidelity_a: Cascade Mountain Tech Trekking Poles - Carbon Fiber Walking or Hiking Sticks with Quick Adjustable Locks These poles come with a lightweight, durable zippered carrying case and four (8 total) pole end attachments for leaves, snow, blunt-end, and curved trekking. All the attachments alone are accessories that you have to purchase separately with many more expensive pole sets. The snow and leaf attachments are plastic, screwed onto the poles with threads, and the other two are rubber push-on. These are a single-clamp design for length adjustment and compact storage. They have very nice, comfortable wrist straps. With the extensions retracted, their stored length is 31 inches. They have carbide tips at the ends of the poles and the grips are a firm foam material. I love the “lower grip” on each pole, which is great for when you are trekking steep uphills and need to grip the poles in a lower position, or if you are traversing side-hill and need one pole shorter on the uphill side. I can tell you that these poles are extremely light at 5.5 ounces per pole. I have a set of CMT poles that are a two-clamp design at 7.6 ounces each. I can honestly say, in the whole of all of my hiking/backpacking equipment, I know of no other equipment that delivers the quality and light weight compared to price as these poles. There are few items I know of that are more deserving of the five stars that I give these poles

KOMAN Portable Camping Stove, Backpacking Stove with Piezo Ignition,Butane Stove with Hose, Outdoor Windproof Camp Cooking Stove with Adjustable Burner for Traveling,Hiking (canister not include) I lived through 5 days without power during the Texas blizzard and learned a hard lesson - that I was totally unprepared. So over the last year or so I have made sure that I have lights, cooking and heat options that do not require grid electricity. This is one of my cooking options - I love that it can be used with both propane and butane cannisters. I have both for emergencies and while I have both a propane camp stove and a Little Buddy propane heater, I have the butane cannisters so that if I'm without power longer than a day or two, I still have other ways/methods to cook food. This is a nice little cooker and I'm happy to have a dual-fuel cooker that is easy to store until needed.

Edited Jan 8, 2023: I tried this finally and am disappointed. The small metal pieces that are meant to hold a pot up off the flame on this little burner DO NOT FIT THE SLOTS/HOLES made for them! How stupid is that?!? Without them, you cannot cook on it! The ONLY thing I can use this for is with the little round camping heater that was meant to use with gas-powered burners. Here's the camping heater should you have one like this and want to use it as a heater: https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B07R5VXMRC/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&th=1

text_fidelity_a:
Etekcity Water Filter Straw Camping Water Purification Portable Water Filter Survival Kit for Camping, Hiking, Hurricanes I've had this on my bug-out list for a while now. At last I got it. I had questions I had doubts, because I was at first thinking of this as a filtration system. Yes it filtrates water.... no it is not a general filtration system. It is a "Personal" filter. A sip straw with advantages. Emphasis on the 'sip'. If you got as far as the comments section, you've seen what they say about it. This is for hiking, rather than camping use. Something to get water from point A to your mouth. However.... I did want to find out if I could use the bag to filter water into a cup for heating and it DOES work! You fill the bag with water... as clear as you can find, screw it into the straw, and gently but firmly squeeze. Filtered water will slowly dribble out of the sipping end. Not fast, but if you need a cup of coffee or some soup, it would be worth it. We are not talking kitchen magic here folks, we are talking survival.
To make this last as long as possible, use the clearest water you can find, use the little blue add-on filter, and backwash every time you use it. Just remember, water from a street gutter is not a good source, because of all the chemical contaminates that might be in it. This is for dirt, microbes, and insect contamination, not oil, anti-freeze and cleaners!
Picture 1 shows the bag screwed into the base, 2 shows the long folded tube attached to the base. you can also take off the short tube from the blue filter and attach it to the end of the long tube. Picture 3 shows the blue filter and the disk replacement filters for it (you get 6 total), and 4 shows the back-flow set-up. The plunger tube snugs 'into' not 'over' the mouth piece and the small blue filter's tube as well.

This was one of the Eteckcity products that I could get free or at reduced price in exchange for a review. I won't 'guess' if it works I won't say something I don't believe. This my honest opinion of a product I acquired to use personally.
text_fidelity_b: Etekcity Water Filter Straw Camping Water Purification Portable Water Filter Survival Kit for Camping, Hiking, Hurricanes

text_fidelity_a:
Outerstuff Toddler NFL Piped Raglan Full-Zip Jumper This is made of a light, soft, flame retardant flannel.

It has a long white zipper which goes almost to the toes, with an easy snap at the top.

The fabric is cute with Patriots logo.

It has white stitching for accent.

It is 100% polyester. I prefer cotton which breathes better.

It has two pesky labels at the top back.

You are supposed to turn this inside out when you wash on cold, gentle cycle with like colors. Do not use fabric softener or it will impact flame retardant ability. Non-chlorine bleach. Tumble dry low.

It was made in Bangladesh.

Suggestions for improvement: use more cotton in fabric, substitute print for labels at upper back, and perhaps skip the flame retardant chemicals. 3.5 stars

Here's some info which discourages flame retardant fabrics close to children's skin:
A study published in August 2014 found that PBDEs (polybrominated diphenyl ethers), the most commonly used fire-retardant chemicals, were linked to numerous health problems.

Researchers found the chemicals were to blame for:

thyroid disruption
early onset of puberty
cognitive problems
delayed mental and physical development
“The chemicals used to make pajamas and other consumer products flame-retardant show up in water, wildlife, and human breast milk,” says pediatrician Michael Macknin, MD.

According to Dr. Macknin, the chemicals in fire retardants do diminish the flammability of products treated with them and have been associated with decreased burn injuries in children. However, the chemicals aren’t well-bound to the fabric fibers at times and can leech out. This allows the fire-retardant chemicals to float free in the environment.

“The long-term impact these chemicals may have on health and cognition is not closely scrutinized,” says Dr. Macknin. “They are often put on the market without long-term studies of their safety.”

Other dangers besides pajamas
These chemicals are found in furniture and mattresses as well as cell phones, television remotes and numerous other consumer plastics, says Dr. Macknin.

“If the tag on a sofa or mattress you’re planning to buy says, ‘this article complies with flammability requirements of California Bureau of Home Furnishings Technical Bulletin 117’, or language to that effect, it likely contains pounds of PBDEs,” he says.

You’ll find this sort of notice on numerous children’s products like car seats, strollers, toys and changing mats. According to Dr. Macknin and other health experts, these added chemicals may put your child at a greater risk than the flames they claim to inhibit. An alternative to chemically treated flame-retardant pajamas are close-fitting pajamas made of natural fibers. Some fabrics meet smolder standards without added chemicals.
text_fidelity_b: Outerstuff Toddler NFL Piped Raglan Full-Zip Jumper

text_fidelity_a:
Northwest Double Sided Cloud Soft Plush Throw Blanket 60"x70" My niece is in her second year at Michigan, so my wife and I have been cheering for them. When I saw this Double Sided Cloud Soft Plush Throw Blanket 60"x70" (Michigan Wolverines - Blue,) I decided to grab it for when she visits and for around the house when we're watching football. So far we really like it, we are impressed, but we agreed, we cannot decide if it's deserving of 5 or 4 stars... here's why:

It arrived in a typical bag, so nicely folded and showing off the bright, brilliant colors. This was a plus. When opening it felt super soft instantly and we were thrilled. She's going to love it when she's here. My wife will love it for game days.

The material is great... but we cannot tell if it'll be one of those kinds that sheds or pills after (during) washing. We are not interested in washing it until it needs it, so we're not going to know until then. On the other hand, we shook it out and threw it a few times across the bed and shook it to try and see if something flew off - nothing did. So cool, all is well so far... Then why the continued concern? The stitching along the sides is average at best, really not great overall. For something we should be thrilled with, this weak spot was enough to not sooth our concerns. I try to show this in a couple pictures - all the way around you can see the batting sticking through - why is this and does this lessen the quality? Now you understand why we gave it the 5, but are giving the heads up on a possible 4.

The colors and design are wonderful - it looks great across the bed. And the reverse is just as nice looking. There is a "shadow" blue to the M which looks a bit... weird, but other than that - and it really doesn't dominate - it looks so cool.

So in the end we went with 5, we love the feel, my wife can't wait for cold weather, and my niece will love it ( and yea, don't say anything, but we'll likely get her one for Christmas.
text_fidelity_b: Northwest Double Sided Cloud Soft Plush Throw Blanket 60"x70"

text_fidelity_a:
Wipkal 2 Pcs New Cooling Hat Ice Hat Wide Brim Cap, Summer Sun Hat Sunscreen Cooling Air Conditioning Cap Ice Cap Towel UV Protection for Women Men Light Gray Thought this will beat the traditional hay hats, wrong!
Hat is way too large in diameter. You will catch yourself bumping into everything. Sort of like wearing two numbers larger shoes, try it! it's annoying and so is the round hat, I guarantee you.
Next non-sense with the round hat is the side slits behind the mesh let the sun in. Rating sun protection 1 star as it defies the purpose of why I ended up buying this in first place; and If I posted picturet after first couple hours of wearing it outside in decent yet not extreme heat, you'd be horrified to notice the staining from sweat after it dries, in repeated sessions. It looks disgusting. Fabric, or faux leather, whatever the outer coating is made of, does not give an indication of long lasting life of a product, instead I expect it to peel soon, matter of fact, mesh on one side is already ripping off a good section at the lower seam due to not so precise stitching that skipped the mesh thanks to its large openings. The central insulation material that seem to be the same glossy flex aluminum you see inside the small refrigeration lunch bags is incredibly thin and expected to rip after a year or two of use - IF nothing else rips before it of course. (mesh pun intended)
Finally the inner blue "cooling" fabric that is to be wetted... impressions after handling it is nothing like what one thinks of when ordering this set. Thought it'll be pretty thick to absorb enough liquid to provide lasting cooling effect. What you will get? Another thin layer, to me these words immediately jumped into my mind: "A blue toilet paper, or is it actual fabric?" Yep, those are the impressions and the rating solely for the round hat so far.
I have yet to try the baseball type hat, but I dont see it to be any better except I wont be bumping my head against the firm hat that loves to bump into everything around you. On the other hand, sun protection is limited with baseball type hat as it doesnt cover in entire circle but a small section. Like I said in the headline, I dont know.

text_fidelity_a:
Smooth Fitness Agile DMT Trainer As there are plenty of reviews, I'm going to do a review that assumes you've read the rest and I will try and hit some of the criticisms. I've owned my DMT for about a month and a half. I'm not an overly picky or difficult person, as some reviewers seem to be. Not criticizing them, just letting you know that I may be easier going than you are. I got mine at $2399 so for me this was a bit of an investment and I read all the reviews I could find. Since Smooth only seems to publish the great reviews on their website, I am publishing mine here. I do think the Treadmill Doctor reviews are fair and accurate, but they seem to have a chummy relationship with Smooth.

I ordered the unit and the Smooth Sync Bluetooth module. I ordered it with the white glove service as I'm lazy and it's heavy. First, the ordering process, here is my timeline:

- 12 Jan 13, Order placed with Smooth via web
- 12 Jan 13, Email confirmation of order
- 18 Jan 13, Credit card charged
- 18 Jan 13 Product Shipped Notice
- 27 Jan 13, Contacted by shipping/assembly company
- 28 Jan 13, Product received/assembled
- 29 Jan 13, Smooth Sync received/installed

The unit arrived in one large box and one ridiculously large box. It would have been difficult for my 21 year-old son and I to get it in the house. Unless you are awfully burly or have moving equipment (a standard dolly won't get it) then at least have it delivered to the room where you want to set it up. When assembled, even using the wheels, if I moved it by myself I would be hurting the next day. As others have said, the assembly duo (from CEVA Logistics) had never seen one before, but had assembled similar items. They assembled it correctly without damage to the unit or anything else in about an hour. I'm pretty handy and I think I could have done it a bit quicker. If you assemble it yourself, you are primarily assembling the upright portion. When we tried using it the first time, something was banging. They disassembled one section, reassembled and everything was grand.

Smooth forgot to ship the Smooth Sync so it wasn't available day one, but UPS ground got it here the next day. It installed in just a few minutes with no problems.

I did quite a bit of research before buying. I use ellipticals at the gym and I own a top of the line Bowflex. The Agile DMT replaced a Proform 7.0 Treadmill that gave up the ghost after 14 years and several moves. In terms of engineering, construction and features, there is absolutely no comparison between this and my Proform. This is a gym quality machine with more features than any gym will ever pay for. Contrary to what others have said, the speakers are not bad. The fan is a bit cheap, but on the highest setting it provides a little breeze. The display/control panel is functional but not impressive.

Others commented on all the plastic. While it seems a little silly, it does cover a lot of the moving parts such that you can move around the device without hooking or snagging and it prevents dust and dirt and will make it easier to clean.

As I mentioned, I bought the Smooth Sync. While $130 seems like a lot, if you consider that you are paying for the hardware, the app and the integration, it is not bad. The MySmooth app is good. The video application is interesting, but definitely not something I would pay $20 a video for. It appears Smooth spent quite a lot to shoot the videos. In the current market, they would probably be better off letting users upload their own with the MySmooth app controlling the speed of play. The Android app does not record workouts and accessing the History button crashes the application. Smooth does not have a page with news about the app.

As for customer service, I've never received any response from Smooth that appeared remotely human. It took 6 days to get another email after I placed my order. When the CEVA tracking showed that my machine had been in town for a week and I had received no call, I sent an email to Smooth. I got no reply, but I noted on the bill of lading that Smooth had contacted CEVA and told them to get moving. CEVA called me the day after I sent the email (email Saturday, call Sunday, delivery Monday). When I sent Smooth an email to ask about my Smooth Sync (several weeks after I ordered it) my response was the UPS email notice with no other response. The device arrived the next day via UPS ground. In my book, this is adequate but certainly well below average. I would have expected the order confirmation to provide some type of information on when I could expect a follow-up on shipping. I would have expected them to ship my Smooth Sync so that it was here when the machine arrived. For the price, I would expect at least a follow-up email to see how the delivery/install went and if I had any problems. All of this would really merit a "very good" not an "exceptional" these days. I get follow-up emails from eBay sellers to see if I'm satisfied with a .99 cable.

Smooth was recently purchased. The new owner is continuing the product line and honoring all warranties, etc. Supposedly they are investing millions. Hopefully the person in charge of customer service takes his or her buyout and moves on to be replaced by someone more competent. I say that as I think the products are excellent, so it is too bad when one person brings the company down to simply being good.

As for the white glove delivery install, I live in the DC area. If you don't get experienced assembly people here, odds are you won't elsewhere. My installers got it together with no problems and didn't take all day. I'm satisfied and would do it again.
text_fidelity_b: Smooth Fitness Agile DMT Trainer

infray Hand Warmers, Rechargeable 5200mAh Power Bank Electric Hand Heater USB Portable Charger Double-Sided Heating Pocket Hand Warmer, Safe Heat Therapy Pain Relief Winter Gift for Women Men This is a useful hand warmer for those cold days. It is sized to fit in a pocket, and conveniently recharges with a USB outlet.

I've been using my hand warmer while hunting in the cold November rain. It turns on with a long press of the lone button near the top of the unit. There are 3 heat levels: 35, 45, and 55 degrees C. You can cycle through the 3 levels with short pushes of the control button. The unit heats up quickly, and the display switches automatically to show how much battery is left, once its up to temperature.

The battery, unfortunately, doesn't last very long. At full heat (55 degrees) you get about an hour or two. At the lowest setting, the heater will last longer, but it seems like that depends on how cold the air is where you are using it. If its really cold and you have the heater out and exposed to it, your battery will drain pretty quickly. It will last much longer indoors at room temperature. The lesson here is to keep the heater in your pocket when you can, rather than getting it out and holding it as it warms your hands. If you want it to last all day, turn it on when you need to warm up, then shut it off once you've knocked the chill off. If you only need it to last for an hour or two, to get you through a football game or something like that, you can just let it run.

The recharging port accepts a USB-C plug, the latest format. A charging cord comes with the heater, but there's no adapter to plug it into the wall. Most of us likely have an extra block or two around from our phones or other USB devices.

I wish that the heater was waterproof, or at least weather resistant, to be more useful in really crappy weather. The charging port, for example, is open to the weather so I usually keep the heater in a small ziplock bag when I'm using it in the snow or rain. It works OK that way.

If you haven't used up all the juice in the heater's battery, you can use it to recharge your phone or other USB device. That's a potentially useful utility. I haven't used mine that way yet, though.

The pocket-sized heater works best in a central pocket that you can reach with both hands, like the Joey pouch on the front of a pullover hoodie. If you don't have that, you have to either cradle it in both hands, outside your pockets, to warm both hands at once, or switch it from one pocket to another, to warm your hands one at a time. Another potential use is in the foot of your sleeping bag or bed, to warm your feet, but the heat won't last all night.

Electric heaters in general are notorious for demanding lots of energy. This little heater does produce a nice warm glow in your pocket, but it doesn't seem to have resolved the inherent inefficiency of electric heaters.

Please let me know if you found anything in my review helpful.
text_fidelity_b: infray Hand Warmers, Rechargeable 5200mAh Power Bank Electric Hand Heater USB Portable Charger Double-Sided Heating Pocket Hand Warmer, Safe Heat Therapy Pain Relief Winter Gift for Women Men

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker I'm a Fitbit lover. I track everything with it; steps, heart rate, activity, sleep, food, BMI, body fat. All these metrics warm my geeky little heart and help me achieve my health goals. I own a Flex, an Alta HR, and the Aria 2 scale and have adored all of them. Because I love them so much, I gave my husband a Charge 3 for his birthday. I'm sorry to say, this Fitbit product is a total dud. The tracker will not sync with Fitbit's app. It worked for about 1 month then just stopped syncing with the app. We've tried every flavor of delete-reinstall-reset possible, all to no avail. There are hundreds, maybe thousands, of people who have this same issue, who have reported it to Fitbit, and the response is unfortunately not in keeping with the company's usual excellent customer service. All they will offer people is another Charge 3. You can't even swap the tracker for a less expense, older model that works with their app. Without the app, without the ability to track and review a history, the Charge 3 is little better than the freebie plastic pedometers your employer's health insurance plan hands out at their annual Open Enrollment fair. What's more than a little irksome is that Fitbit seems unwilling to admit there's a major software problem here. Seems obvious when one reads the Help forums. Why not 'fess up and tell us an estimate of when we can expect a software update? I don't get it. People will likely be patient and wait for the update if they know one is in the works. What is to be gained by pretending nothing is wrong? A lot of very unhappy customers, that's what.

Long story short: Don't buy this tracker. Get a different one. Maybe even one not made by Fitbit (sorry, Fitbit!)
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker

My son and his tent mate each had one of these, and they had to reposition their cots so they ran from side to side instead of front to back to avoid downward pressure from the sloping tent roof. The sloping ends of this cot then fit the roofline of the tent very well.

I have slept in this for 3 nights so far and my son has slept in his 6 nights. It seems well made and like it will hold up well.

text_fidelity_a:
Freein Stand Up Paddle Board sup Explorer SUP Inflatable Stand up Paddle Board 10'2"/ 11'x33 x6 Glass Fiber Paddle, Dual Action Pump, Removable Fin, Leash, Dry Bag, Adaptor, Camera Mount, Backpack Got this on prime day after a friend had been doing tons of research and was going to buy two of these, I figured for $280 I could take a chance as well. Before taking it out I pumped it up to check it out and its a monster. It is thick....really thick. If you're only experienced with fiberglass surfboards or SUP boards you'll be surprise how thick this is when you pump it up. I think its even thicker than a lot of inflatable boards, but I honestly haven't studied many up close or taken a tape measure to them, so who knows. Anyway, just for giggles I put one end on the couch and the other on a chair, with the middle totally unsupported, and got on. It held my 180lbs only bending an inch or two which impressed me. It left me wondering why we didn't buy one or two of these sooner.

So I finally was able to take it out on the lake and it took me about 5min to pump it up - I was going fast and wanted to push myself. I forgot to put the bigger fin in, and the wind was a constant 5-10mph with gusts to 25mph. Without that fin I definitely had tracking issues and could only get 2-3 strokes per side before I was turning one way or the other. I can't say for sure, but really think it would've been much easier if I had put that fin in....oh well. Its pretty light, the D rings are pretty strong, and I'm super confident it can hold a ton of weight (my friend put himself, his wife, and his kid on it in calm waters and had no issues).

A couple of concerns:
its a little bigger than it needs to be,
it didn't come with the patch glue, just the patch,
in time I could see abrasions from parking lots, sand, rocks, branches/logs, etc. breaking it down quickly (and any other inflatable),
and I already have a little ding in it. I'm not sure how it happened because I don't remember hitting any rocks and don't think its from the parking lot or sand, but so far it isn't impacting its ability to hold air.

In the future I wouldn't hesitate to buy another one of these, but might look for one thats smaller and less bulky.
text_fidelity_b: Freein Stand Up Paddle Board sup Explorer SUP Inflatable Stand up Paddle Board 10'2"/ 11'x33 x6 Glass Fiber Paddle, Dual Action Pump, Removable Fin, Leash, Dry Bag, Adaptor, Camera Mount, Backpack

text_fidelity_a: Mobihome Hydration Backpack & 2L Leak Proof Water Hydration Bladder,Lightweight Running Backpack & Hydration Pack, Running, Hiking, Cycling, Climbing,Skiing for Men Women & Kids, Airflow Camel Pack This "Mobihome" hydration backpack is wonderful! In the past, we had bought one for our youngest son, and he raved about his. So...I ordered this hydration backpack for myself. I go hiking in the Wyoming hills with my BFF occasionally and it seems I always run out of water before we get return. This backpack holds 2 liters of water so I have plenty for a day hike. Also there's these little rubber ice cubes you can put in the freezer the night before and have cold water all day. Just make sure the rubber ice cubes have no sharp edges. The bite value you pull up to open and push down to close. The water bag inside the backpack has a harder plastic handle that you slide off to expose the water bladder to fill it up or drain/clean. Make sure this water bladder is completely drained and dry before you close it again or you could have mold next time. There are additional zipper pockets for cell phones, bandages, anti-bacterial cream, bug repellent, an extra pair of clean socks and shorts/pants, and your breakfast and/or lunch. Perfect for a day hike. The main storage area at first was difficult for me to find as it sits inside an oval shaped fabric trim. Plenty of room in their for clothing and/or lunch, beef jerky, and any snacks you bring along with you. There's also braided elastic bungee cords on the back that you could use to hold a small blanket or an extra pair of shoes and even a small tent. It does unhook so you can tie your item down. Each side has mesh pockets. I usually put canned/bottled pop in mine but others like to take along a can/bottle of beer. There's a yellow rainproof cover to keep everything dry. The shoulder straps are nice and large with an orange snap closure. And there's a black snap closure strap for around your waist. This lightweight backpack fits snug to your body and if it wasn't for the weight of the water, you'd probably not even notice you had it on. I hope to get more hikes in this summer. However, it's already getting pretty hot even in the mornings. So next time we'll need to find a place to hike that has lots of tree's for shade. This hydration backpack is holding up very well.

text_fidelity_a:
Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack-Red-L I love this backpack! I commute by bike, and I wear those ridiculous spandex biking togs to keep cool whilst riding and not get my work clothes sweaty. Rather than packing a change of clothes every day, I take a week's worth of clothes in on Mondays. I like having the clothes in a backpack to I can easily take them to the restroom in the mornings to change, and keep the rest of them out of sight during the day. I was using a regular backpack, but that added weight, which is not great for biking, and it added bulk, meaning it was hard to fit everything in my pannier - I had to really stuff it in there and struggle a bit to fasten down the pannier's straps.

I bought this backpack in the hopes it would contain my clothes without excess weight or bulk. It's perfect! I have the 33L (largest) size, and it easily holds: 1 pair of (large) jeans, 5 shirts, 5 pairs of underwear, a couple of bras, a few pairs of socks, a microfiber washcloth and a small pack towel, with a bit of room to spare. It weighs virtually nothing, and adds almost no bulk, so now a week's worth of clothes fits easily in my pannier and doesn't weigh my bike down any more than absolutely necessary.

Since I have it at work anyway, I've used it to transport my laptop and other items, and it's plenty strong enough, and has enough useful pockets, to be an everyday backpack. My only small complaint would be that it lacks any structure. But that is, of course, by design, as it's meant to be folded up into a small package when not in use. But I never fold it up because I use it almost every day.

This was a great purchase. Very good value, high quality product, perfect for my needs.
text_fidelity_b: Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack-Red-L

text_fidelity_a:
Esbit Ultralight Folding Pocket Stove with Six 14g Solid Fuel Tablets steel, Small - Original Used this during a 2 day hike in a cave in the southeastern US. At ambient 58F near ~2,100' AMSL, 1 Esbit 14g fuel tablet just brings 1.5l of water to a boil before burning out. They claim 12 min. burn time. I only observed around 8~9 min, but it did what I needed, was smaller and lighter than propane canisters, etc. Fuzzy guess says the cost per pot heated is similar to propane, with these being a bit more trouble/less flexible, but smaller and lighter.

Compared to Trioxane, these tablets seem to have about ~30% more energy per tablet, but that's just this backpacker's impression. They're harder to light than trioxane, but not overly difficult.

This little stove has a slightly wider base than the old US Army issue Trioxane stoves. This makes balancing a pot on it much easier. Note that canteen cups don't balance well -- it's just a bit too wide for them to fit comfortably. You can sort of jam one in, but it's precarious and falls over if you so much as sneeze at it. This makes sneezing at your canteen cup highly discommended. A great loss, to be sure.
text_fidelity_b: Esbit Ultralight Folding Pocket Stove with Six 14g Solid Fuel Tablets steel, Small - Original

text_fidelity_a: Ultimate Body Press Ceiling Mount Pull Up Bar for 8 Foot Ceilings, Steel Through-Bolted 48” Straight Bar with 14” Risers, Fits 16”and 24” Joist Spacing, Max 450lbs, USA Designed and Backed I installed a pull up bar using pipes from a hardware store previously.  The issue was weakness at the pipe threads.  Because I was concerned about getting injured, I shopped around and this was the only I could find for around 100$ that had a non-moving bar.  I also wanted a simple single bar, not a double bar. The pros are it is easy to install, it doesn’t budge, even when I (accidentally) kip. I weight 220 pounds, so that says a lot.  The bar is appropriate length and circumference for a proper grip.  I am 5’7 and installed on 9 foot rafters it’s perfect. I need to hop up or use small step.  This is good, as I don’t want my feet to touch the ground. The screws, nuts and bolts are correct. The disadvantage is it’s expensive for what it is, three pieces of painted metal and some nuts and bolts with a greasy wrench and hex..  The “wrench” is kind a joke,  it It can be used.  A drill bit would have been more useful. The grip is too smooth, like most pull up bars. Like most fitness equipment, grips are either too smooth, or knurled to the point they rip up your hands. I use tennis ratchet grips (it took six) to wrap it.  It is probably a foot too wide, not an issue, as you could attach accessories to the extra space and do really wide pull ups. It would be helpful for it to include a cutout on the box for install.  You definitely need another person or straps to install it. Time will tell, but it’s great so far.  I do think it’s a bit expensive for what it is, but nothing else really compares.  The inconveniences are minor, so would recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Ultimate Body Press Ceiling Mount Pull Up Bar for 8 Foot Ceilings, Steel Through-Bolted 48” Straight Bar with 14” Risers, Fits 16”and 24” Joist Spacing, Max 450lbs, USA Designed and Backed

text_fidelity_a:
Igloo Ice Cube, Ocean Blue, 14-can Capacity, 32607 ORIGINAL REVIEW: I replaced my previous Igloo cooler with this one and I really like it. The top compartment is handy. I put a camper type salt shaker in it along with a few other small items. The ice packs that I use fit perfectly and so far the handle seems like it will last. The previous igloo cooler was a bit smaller and was bought in 1992. It still works great except the handle wont stay on so it was time for a new one. I mention this because it's 24 years old and still works. that says a lot for igloo quality. I hope to get that kind of service from this cooler. The only reason the handle failed was because I stumbled and sent the cooler flying. If that had not have happened I probably would not have needed to buy this one. Igloo is rugged, last a long time and with 2 ice packs about the same size as the sides of this cooler, everything stays cool for at least 24 hours as long as it's not in direct sunlight. I'm not one for change, especially when I have a product that works and lasts. I really did need a little larger cooler so yes, I miss the old cooler but not so much because I really like this new one much better. I donated the old one and found it good home. Yes I know it's just a cooler but I used t every work day for 24 years, I got a little attached to it. They still make that model and I nearly bought it but my wife found this new one. Due to the handle issue and the fact this one is way better, I do not recommend the older version any longer in favor for this one. Yes I know run on sentences its 1 am give me a break. Buy this cooler, slap a Cowboys sticker on it and you will be happy with it.

UPDATE: Guess I was wrong about the handle lasting, it didn't. I still use it for now but plan on replacing it with a similar cooler called Igloo Quantum. This may be an updated version of the ice cube model who knows. The handle feels better but attaches the same so i expect it to fail as well. It has a few additional features like 2 places to put a lock or locks on it, useless because it can be easily cut. 2 cup holders that I find too shallow to be useful and the top compartment is half the size. The cover is thicker and opens easier from the center as opposed to the corners like the ice cube model. Lastly; it's 3 tone. Had I know the Quantum was available I would have purchased it over the ice cube model. In my opinion, they should lose the cup holders and increase the top compartment size, ensure the handle wont come off and you would have a great cooler.
text_fidelity_b: Igloo Ice Cube, Ocean Blue, 14-can Capacity, 32607

text_fidelity_a: Yukon Charlie's Sherpa Snowshoe My husband and I have been snowshoeing for fifty years, but at 77, we find we can't break trail the way we used to, and the older bindings and the full-size snowshoes are too cumbersome. Over the years we've downsized from the old wooden Bean snowshoes, through the Tubbs 36-inch shoes, and after much research and try-ons, we settled on these Sherpas. We've used them for a year now and are very pleased. They're short enough and light but still track well through half a foot or more of new snow. The crampons grip well on hills or crust, and the bindings are amazingly easy to use. We did find we had to use thin wire or twist-ties to clamp the heel strap back on itself, otherwise the small metal tongue will pop out of the adjustment hole. In cold and and snow, having the heel strap loosen was an issue, but wiring it tight was the solution.

text_fidelity_a:
LANGNING Ultralight Badminton Racket Set, 9U 62gram Tension Full Carbon Fiber Black Badminton Racquet(Air9U Plus) My wife has been wanting us to get into badminton more, but the place (club) we visit sometimes only has lower end rackets, so when I had the chance to grab this LANGNING Ultralight Badminton Racket Set, 9U 62gram Tension Full Carbon Fiber I took it (for her). She'd played in high school and was looking for something very light and that would be a higher quality. The racket itself is excellent and so far she really likes it. I was able to get another brand for myself (here on Amazon), and in a side-by-side comparison this LANGNING Ultralight Badminton Racket Set, 9U 62gram Tension Full Carbon Fiber is by far the lighter one. Now when I say 'by far' it is of course relative. If you were to pick up either on it's own you'd have no idea something that "light" could be SO LIGHT, but they both are - separately - then when holding one each - wow this LANGNING Ultralight Badminton Racket Set, 9U 62gram Tension Full Carbon Fiber shows off its lighter weight! Who knew. It looks great, if that's important to you. It has a great grip and both of us feel extremely comfortable holding it. The head is where the action is, and to our non-professional knowledge, it too is excellent. We've only played a pick up game at home since it arrived, but it was fun, easy for her to use, and gave her everything she was looking for - there was a definite improvement over what we've been using at the club. So far, so good, and she loves the racket.

There is one... "downside" to this LANGNING Ultralight Badminton Racket Set: the "set" part, in comparison to the set I grabbed for myself, is lesser-than. This LANGNING Ultralight Badminton Racket Set only has the racket and the bag, but even the bag is less-than; a cloth bag with the logo on it. Nothing more to see here. For the price of the set we thought it would be a big more impressive, but they put their money where the racket is, not the "set." text_fidelity_a:
Crosman American Classic Pump Air Pistol (.177) Back in 1977 I purchased one of the first models of this pistol, and used it for years. Around 2003 I lost it. Long story short I loaned it to someone and never got it back. Guessing you know the moral to that story.

Just recently I've gotten the urge to do some target shooting in my back yard - I can probably blame watching episodes of [[ASIN:B003NX6C1C Top Shot]] for that. So I wanted to replace my 1377, mainly because I still had all the accessories for it. So I got on Amazon and found this one to purchase.

To be honest, I did not read the information on the product page - just ordered it. A few days later I had the pistol in my hands. First thing I noticed is it's not quite the gun I remember having. Apparently the design has been changed. Gone was the pull knob that you used to cock the gun and instead there is a breach mechanism. I think I actually like the new design better.

One of the biggest surprise for me was that this model no longer makes use of Bbs. Gone is the magnetic tip on the end of loading pin. Wish I had know that before including this package in my order - [[ASIN:B000HKKY7M Crosman Copperhead 6000 Copper Coated BBs in a Bottle]]. But, that is my fault for not paying attention to what was on the product page.

Anyway - even just shooting pellets I am having fun with this gun. I also bought packs of these pellets - [[ASIN:B001DCB61Q Crosman Destroyer .177 Cal, 7.9 Grains, Pointed, 250ct]] & [[ASIN:B002DM0ZIU Crosman Hollow Point Pellets, 0.177-Calibre]]. Both seem to work well.

I've been having a lot of fun plinking cans and shooting targets. I think this pellet gun is great.
text_fidelity_b: Crosman American Classic Pump Air Pistol (.177)

text_fidelity_a:
Camp Chef Rainier Grill and Portable Camp Stove When I purchased the unit I thought it came with the griddle too. It doesn't. I thought I'd be able to buy the griddle separately but it was readily apparent it was not available from Camp Chef or anywhere else. I thought about returning the unit because the aluminum grill material will not hold a pot or a griddle without being damaged. If you are looking to buy the stove make sure you get the Camp Chef Ranier Combo which includes the griddle. For some reason though the Combo stove is 40% more expensive than the base Ranier Grill Camp stove. It is for that reason I passed on returning what I had purchased and looked for a cheaper jury-rigged solution.

We solved the grill limitations by purchasing a $12 BBQ rectangle expansion grate from a local hardware warehouse. I removed the expansion arms and cut off two of the grates from one end with an angle grinder, but left the grate supports so the gratefree end had about a 2" extension on each side. The extensions fit nicely under the single burner grate and the adapted grill perfectly covered the grilling section of the stove. The adapted grate moves a little, but very little. We can use the grill section now for a griddle we already own or an additional pot. You cannot use the adapted grill for grilling though because the gas burner element in the grilling section is not protected from fat drippings. When we want to grill, we just remove the adapted grill and replace it with the original grill that came with the stove because it has the burner element protector built down the center of the grill.

Now, having said all that, we love the stove. We use it with the bulk hose adapter for a 20 lb propane bottle. The single burner quickly boils water and is relatively adjustable for pot/pan cooking. The stove burners light with one or two clicks of the lighter button. If all I wanted was the grill and stove I would have given it 5 stars, but the fact that the combo unit is so much more expensive and the griddle is not available as a separate purchase, resulting in a jury-rig solution, I gave it four stars
text_fidelity_b: Camp Chef Rainier Grill and Portable Camp Stove

text_fidelity_a:
Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer Download the manual from the Burley website.

This is our second Travoy trailer. The other is still in use after 10 years. The new Travoy has some substantial upgrades:

• The new “kickstand” design keeps the trailer upright when parked with a load. The old one would tip over.
• New seatpost hitch allows a single hitch to be shared among two or more bikes. With the old one you had to buy more hitches.
• The tow arm now extends to accommodate rear bike racks and larger MTB wheels.
• Tow arm is now padded with foam for hand comfort.

The entire time we owned our first Travoy we mistakenly believed we should have chosen a flatbed instead. We recently bought a flatbed and don’t use it; bought a second Travoy as a backup. If all you do is local errands the Travoy is by far the easiest and best. If you tour or travel dirt roads a flatbed might be a better choice but you should want both a flatbed plus the Travoy because the Travoy is easier for local errands which are far more common.

The bags that are dedicated for use with the Travoy are costly and do not hold enough. Instead, wheel your Travoy into Target or Walmart and choose the largest clothes hamper that fits the Travoy form factor (see photo). Attach that hamper with three ratcheting tie-downs or four high quality, ADJUSTABLE bungees. Do not skimp on quality or number.

PROS:
• Lightweight, 10lbs +/-
• No tools or setup required. Screw the hitch onto your seatpost with the T-bold and you’re done.
• Folds to easily fit in a backseat, a trunk or an airline overhead.
• Holds up to $125 in groceries with the large hamper attached. Mind the maximum weight restriction (60lbs) and pack the heaviest items at the bottom (66% of load) and lighter items at the top (33%).
• With the Travoy you don’t have to bend over quite as far to reach cargo.
• Comes with a storage/carrying bag (although it’s mostly useless for carrying cargo).

CONS:
• You must adjust your riding style slightly. The Travoy is stable on level pavement but may tip over at significant road imperfections or surface debris. Slow down and approach handicapped ramps and driveways exactly at 90 degrees (perpendicular) to avoid catching a wheel on their raised shoulders. Avoid potholes and debris entirely. You’ll grow accustomed to this over time and it will not bother you. If the Travoy DOES tip, it doesn’t take the bike with it.
• If you run with the stock tires and tubes be prepared for flats. The availability of high quality 12.5” inch tires and tubes is extremely limited. All the tires from Asia that we tried are no good, even dangerous. We found very high quality 12.5 inch tires from the German manufacturer “Schwalbe” (available here on Amazon). Schwalbe currently offers the “Road Cruiser” for street and the “Black Jack” for trails and off-road (12/2020).
• 12.5” thorn resistant tubes are available here on Amazon but the Travoy 12.5 inch wheels require a 45 degree valve; otherwise there is not enough room to attach a pump or even a pump hose. These thorn resistant tubes had straight valves. To accommodate this shortcoming we found a "Air Inflator Hose Adapter" here on Amazon. Although it just barely fits, we can use it with both our floor pump and our road pump.

TIPS:
• In addition to thorn resistant tubes, we use the “Mr. Tuffy”-brand tire inserts on all our bike and trailer wheels (here on Amazon). Flats are now a very rare occurrence and we ride among numerous desert thorns.
• When using the hamper it is easy to cut a neon yellow reflective vest into three sections (left front, right front and back) and attach the sections to the hamper (left side, right side and rear, see photo).
• Reflective flags and flagpoles with mounts that fit your hamper are available here on Amazon. The flagpole we bought is high enough so that the flag can be seen above the level of a parked car (see photo). For added safety we now use this flag and pole on our bikes even without the trailer.
• When the hamper is inappropriate we use a cargo net. The cargo net is also handy if your hamper is overflowing.

Leave a comment if you have questions.
text_fidelity_b: Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer

text_fidelity_a:
High Limb Brand CS-48 Rope-and-Chain Saw At first this seemed like a good item. I practiced with 2 small branches close to the ground and was surprised how quickly it cut.

Then I decided to move on and tackle the ones I needed gone. Unlike so many others reviewing, I had no problems getting the blade to flip the right way. I used a simple lasso style toss and made suree the metal weight was facing the right way before the chain reached the branch.

The first branch went fine but I realized I did need to figure out a way to undercut the bigger ones I was going to work on before moving on and cutting them. The suggestion in the manual is pretty useless: you can't just stand to one side and undercut if you're trying to cut something 15-20 feet in the air, at best you'll cut at about a 45 angle. This meant I was going to need to cut the branches in a multitude of cuts to avoid the weight of a partially cut branch pinching the chain as it started to cut.

The first few cuts using this method worked. Then the inevitable happened: the chain got pinched and stuck. I tried the common sense solution of simply throwing the weight bag back over the opposite way to try and relieve the bind and wiggle it free while someone else put some force on the branch. The good news was the branch ended up breaking this way. The bad news: the chain broke too.

There appears to be absolutely no way to repair the chain supplied in this kit. There are no spare rivets or links supplied to perform what has to be a very common issue. This means you basically have just spent $40ish for two 25' pieces of nylon (that btw aren't even finished at the ends so they unravel), a bean bag, 2 "handle straps" that are next to useless and a clear plastic case marked "Made in the USA". And it pretty much looks like there is no warranty, replacement parts or even customer service of any kind.

I'd have to think anyone thinking of needing one of these rope saws can make one with a baseball drilled and with a string strung through it, 50' of nylon from your local hardware store and a replacement chain for any brand chain saw. And that too would be "Made in the USA".
text_fidelity_b: High Limb Brand CS-48 Rope-and-Chain Saw

text_fidelity_a: Thule AllTrail X Hiking Backpack This pack weighs in at 2.04lbs. Not the lightest in its price range, but not bad. It’s pretty minimalistic in features, but has most of what you’d need for a pack its size. The one thing I noticed immediately is that there is very little padding in the shoulder straps. There are lower shoulder strap adjusters, which are nice, but I’d really like to have seen more padding in the shoulder straps. There are adjustable chest and waist straps. Where many backpacks have a wide waist strap, this one is 3/4 inch wide. I have seen, however, that a lot of packs in this size have thinner waist straps. The padding section of the waist strap, next to the pack itself, does not have zippered compartments, but for me, I normally wear cargo pants anyway, so that’s no big deal. Again, it’s all somewhat relative to the size of the pack and what its intended use is. This is not a “long haul, heavy load” pack. It has a very nice drawstring enclosure at the top of the pack with a very nice, wide opening. There is a “lid” on top to cover the opening of the pack that is a zippered compartment with plenty of easy-access room to necessities for a day hike. It is secured with a clasp and not a latch, which was a little unusual, but it seems to work fine. Honestly, the hook clasp has less chance of failure than a plastic latch. There is a decent size stuff compartment on the outside of the pack with adjusters at the top. It has two water bottle holders on the bottom sides, which was not easily seen in the photos online. Inside the pack is the divider that will hold a 15” laptop, or a hydration bladder, and it has a latch at the top to secure the bladder in place. There is an opening at the top of the pack specifically designed for the hydration tube. There is no clasp on the shoulder straps to secure the tube. There is also a nice, strong woven handle at the top of the pack. One thing pretty cool are the long side access zippers so as to access things like a rain jacket without having to open the whole pack to get to it. These zippers are not rain resistant, it doesn’t appear. The material that the pack is made of appears to be extremely durable. I can’t attest to its water resistance, but the notes indicate that it’s more resistant than most waxed canvas packs. Time will tell. The back pad is, again, minimal and marginal on ventilation. It has some extra loops and a special loop to hold hiking poles. This is a nice pack and has a lot to like, but unfortunately the overall comfort of the pack is lacking.  Made in Vietnam.
text_fidelity_b: Thule AllTrail X Hiking Backpack

text_fidelity_a: BBAhandware 27.7x18.2x16 in Folding Table Portable Large Camping Table Ultra Light Folding Beach Table Camping with Carrying Bag,Withstands Weights of Up to 55lbs (Silver) I'm not a serious prepper or anything, but I did live 5 days last February without power during the blizzard in Texas.  I have spent the subsequent months getting ready for another time like that again.  The video I watched was a cool way to heat an area in your house when the power is off.  I already had the rectangular paving stones/bricks to place on this table as well as the little alcohol burners.  The idea is to place the cement stones/bricks (the flat ones, not the large ones with holes in them) around the alcohol burner.  The alcohol burner transfers heat to the bricks which in turn release the stored heat over a longer time in the area where they are set up.  Obviously this can't be set up on the floor, so a table that can handle the stored heat is what I needed.  I set the cement blocks up on this metal camping table, put the alcohol burner in the middle and let it "work."  This camping table is the perfect size for my emergency room warming set up with the bricks an burner.  I know it will work fine for a table to use my propane cookstove on as well, but for the moment it is in an emergency box in my house along with the cement bricks and the alcohol burner (and a bottle of rubbing alcohol).  I'm very happy with how this table worked out for my purposes.
text_fidelity_b: BBAhandware 27.7x18.2x16 in Folding Table Portable Large Camping Table Ultra Light Folding Beach Table Camping with Carrying Bag,Withstands Weights of Up to 55lbs (Silver)

Unfortunately, road vibrations cause the light to shut off. Before I gave up on this light, I tried to keep it on by checking every 10-15 seconds on my 20-minute ride to work. I had to turn the light back on at least 20 times. So aggravating! At least the crappy $10 lights stay on!

I give it 2 stars due to Fortified's stellar customer service. I wrote them about the issue and they mailed me some rubber bumpers to help hold the battery inside the housing. The reason the light shorts out is because the battery slides loosely into a chamber with the light bulb connection at the base. Amazingly minor road vibrations break the battery-bulb connection and the light shuts off, and doesn't come back on.

Fortified has refunded my purchase, which I really appreciate. I believe there is a chance I received a defective product. I cannot say this for sure, as I was offered rubber bumpers instead of a full replacement.

Check one of these out at your local bike shop, and make sure they have a refund policy.

text_fidelity_a:
Propper Men's Packable Waterproof Jacket My husband tried this rain jacket on tonight and loves it. Features he loves about it:

* Long - the length is longer than most of his other jackets so protects him more against the rain.

* Zips bottom to top - not over the head which is annoying. You zip from the bottom up to your chin.

* Very large exterior and interior pockets - the 2 exterior pockets near your waist and hips are deep and you can zip them shut so good to put keys, phone, wallet etc. inside and they won't get wet or fall out. There are two upper pockets near your chest which have a flap to keep water out. Inside there are two deep pockets near your waist and hips - 6 pockets total! Lots of room to carry items.

* Navy color - won't show soil easily, and goes with all colors of pants.

* Light weight - not a heavy jacket so you can wear it in the summer, too, on rainy days. Easy to pack and carry.

* Elastic at hem and bottom of sleeves - elastic is loose but gives a little stretch so should fit many sizes. It's also gathered so should keep water out at end of sleeves.

My husband is about 6 feet and weighs about 180. The large fits him well with a little room to spare. The lining is a shiny fabric. There is no tie at the chin. It just zips up to under your chin.

We will test this on a rainy day, and report back if it's not water-proof, but it looks like it should do a great job keeping you dry.

There is a slight scent from the fabric which should dissipate as it airs out. It smells like nylon.

My husband was thrilled with this jacket when he put it on. We've had a LOT of rain in the northeast this spring and summer - 4-5 days a week! - so this jacket will come in handy.
text_fidelity_b: Propper Men's Packable Waterproof Jacket

text_fidelity_a:
Bearwill Golf Net, 10x7ft Heavy Duty Golf Practice Net with Golf Mat, Target Cloth, 8 Golf Tees, 6 Golf Balls, Carry Bag, Golf Training Net for Backyard Driving Chipping Indoor Outdoor Training It didn't take me long to figure out how to assemble it, even if there were no instructions. The description says this is heavy duty, and that's why I got it. Not the best golfer in the world, I wanted something that would withstand the chaos and natural disaster that constitutes my golf swing.

It comes with several soft golf balls to hit into the net. This is fine and dandy, but nothing quite replaces the feel of hitting a real, live (so to speak) golf ball. So, I broke out the real buggers and begin hitting into the net. So far, I've hit probably a thousand balls into the net. It's held up well. I leave it assembled and outside, and it's held up to the weather decently. A stiff wind WILL knock it over, however.

As to heavy duty, that's why I only gave it 4 stars. I've hit several of my typical errant shots right off the back bar brace that runs along the back of the net. It's but a nice little dent--a reminder of my burgeoning skills--complete with the golf ball dimples. Currently, I have two such dents. It seems to be holding up despite the abuse, but I expected something called "heavy duty" to withstand such impacts with a yawn and a sheepish grin. No such luck.

One of my spectacularly mishits (again using a real golf ball) hit the back bar with enough force and with the right angle that it deflected over my head and landed on the roof of my house. Hmmm. I was the one with the sheepish grin, yes sir.

I do put two bricks on the sides to keep the net firmly anchored. It does come with its own anchors, but I wasn't able to use them because the ground upon which it sits is too rocky. Not the golf net's problem. That one is my Arizona yard's personal demon. You might not have such a problem.

The hitting mat is awkward in my opinion, being so small, and unless it is anchored it will certainly move when you strike the ball, which is irritating. I even tried to anchor it, but my trench digging golf swings soon uprooted it, much to my annoyance. Also, it will raise the ball up slightly unnaturally, so you will need to find something else to stand on to make sure it is the same height as the mat. Nope, not for me. I bought a 4x5 mat that I could stand on.

Over all, I recommend this net!
text_fidelity_b: Bearwill Golf Net, 10x7ft Heavy Duty Golf Practice Net with Golf Mat, Target Cloth, 8 Golf Tees, 6 Golf Balls, Carry Bag, Golf Training Net for Backyard Driving Chipping Indoor Outdoor Training

text_fidelity_a:
Mirrycle Incredibell Original Bicycle Bell So far, this is a great bell! I just installed it today after I received it in the mail. It looks and fits great on my 2022 Trek Marlin 6. I was in my garage checking out the new bell and ringing it a few times while my wife was about 40 feet away outside in the driveway talking with her friend who was parked in the driveway with her car running and they both said that they could easily hear the bell. Her friend was in her car and my wife was standing outside the car, mind you, that car was not quite with the cooling fans running and the wind was also blowing to create extra noise. Yes, this bell is plenty loud to get someone's attention. This bell also allows you to rotate the dinger in any position you want, which gives you the ability to position exactly where it is best for you. You just rotate the assembly below the bell and put it how you want it. This is a very well thought out design that works great!

Another example later that evening, I was riding down a pathway that parallels the roadway and as I was approaching a parking lot driveway, there were two vehicles stopped waiting to exit to the roadway. I decided to continue down the pathway between the rear of one vehicle and the front of the other vehicle. But just to make sure that the second car saw me coming, I slowed and chimed the bell three times to get her attention as I was approaching about 25 feet away. She looked up and at me, smiled and waved as I slowly rode between the two vehicles. The bell worked as designed. The construction seems to be sturdy, but time will tell. I would recommend this to anyone looking for a small bell that does the job.
text_fidelity_b: Mirrycle Incredibell Original Bicycle Bell
